france24fr.description: Une équipe de France "sans Français" : l'ex-Premier ministre conservateur espagnol Mariano Rajoy a déclenché un tollé en France, à deux jours de la demi-finale de Coupe du monde contre l'Espagne. Récit France 2.

france24fr.title: Dix mois avant l'élection présidentielle en France, Marine Le Pen en tête dans les sondages
france24fr.description: Dix mois avant la présidentielle française de 2027, Marine Le Pen domine largement le premier tour, donnée entre 34 et 35,5% selon ses concurrents, Jean-Luc Mélenchon se rapprochant d'Édouard Philippe pour une qualification au second tour, selon un sondage Elabe pour BFMTV et la Tribune dimanche. Analyse de Flore Simon, chroniqueuse politique France 24.

france24fr.title: "La Bataille De Gaulle" au cinéma : le succès des deux films sur Charles De Gaulle au box-office
france24fr.description: "La Bataille De Gaulle" fait de la résistance au box-office. Ces deux films de 2h40 trouvent un écho notamment au sein de la nouvelle génération. Comment l'expliquer ? Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: France : immersion à bord du "Tigre", ces hélicoptères franco-allemands qui défileront le 14 juillet
france24fr.description: J-1 avant le dernier défilé du 14 juillet présidé par Emmanuel Macron : immersion à bord du "Tigre", l'un des appareils de combat les plus redoutables de l'armée française. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: France : la Coalition des volontaires en sommet à Paris en présence de Volodymyr Zelensky
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron réunit ce 13 juillet à Paris un sommet de la coalition des volontaires pour l'Ukraine, en présence de Volodymyr Zelensky, signe du "réveil stratégique" souhaité pour l'Europe face à la Russie et aux Etats-Unis de Donald Trump. Analyse de Gauthier Rybinski, chroniqueur international France 24.

france24fr.title: Les États-Unis frappent l'Iran, Téhéran riposte en ciblant des bases du Golfe
france24fr.description: Les hostilités se poursuivent entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran, l'armée ⁠américaine ayant déclaré dimanche ​soir mener de nouveaux bombardements avec l'objectif annoncé d'enrayer les capacités militaires iraniennes près du détroit d'Ormuz, tandis que Téhéran a ciblé des sites militaires américains dans le Golfe. france24fr.title: Espagne : le bilan de l'incendie en Andalousie s'alourdit à treize morts
france24fr.description: L'incendie dans le sud de l'Espagne est "stabilisé", a annoncé le président de la région Juan Manuel Moreno. Le bilan s'est alourdi à 13 morts après le décès d'une Britannique de 93 ans qui était hospitalisée à Almería. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: France : huit cent hectares incendiés à Fontainebleau, deux avions bombardiers déployés
france24fr.description: Deux avions bombardiers d'eau Canadair ont été déployés pour lutter contre les feux qui touchent le sud de la Seine-et-Marne, notamment la forêt de Fontainebleau, massif boisé en proie depuis dimanche à un incendie d'une "ampleur exceptionnelle" selon les autorités.

france24fr.title: En direct : la France prête à défendre "la liberté et le droit", "au prix du sang s'il le faut", dit Macron

france24fr.title: Vacances des Français : le boom des "coolcations"
france24fr.description: La canicule, l'inflation et les tensions géopolitiques transforment les habitudes des vacanciers. Les Français continuent de partir, mais réservent plus tard, privilégient la France et recherchent davantage de fraîcheur.

france24fr.title: En Corée du Sud, l'ex-président Yoon accumule les peines de prison
france24fr.description: Un tribunal a condamné, ​lundi, l'ancien président de la Corée du Sud, Yoon Suk-yeol, à deux ans de prison pour corruption. france24fr.title: Sam Neill, star de "Jurassic Park" et "La leçon de piano", est mort à 78 ans
france24fr.description: L'acteur néo-zélandais Sam Neill, connu pour ses rôles dans "Jurassic Park" et "La Leçon de piano", est décédé à l'âge de 78 ans, a annoncé, lundi, sa famille.

france24fr.description: Jannik Sinner garde sa couronne. L’Italien a remporté Wimbledon pour la deuxième année consécutive après sa victoire en cinq sets contre l’Allemand Alexander Zverev, vainqueur de Roland-Garros début juin. observador.description: É a primeira vez que aviões de combate a incêndios do sul do país são enviados para atuar na região de Paris. Já foram retiradas 900 pessoas das suas casas.

observador.title: Saúde. Privado e Público só em "complementaridade"
observador.description: Na semana em que o Parlamento discute o Estado da Nação, Miguel Guimarães (PSD), Susana Correia (PS) e Marta Silva (CH) discutem o estado do setor da saúde em Portugal.

observador.title: 10h. PS apela a reflexão do Governo sobre reforma na Saúde
observador.description: A deputada socialista Susana Correia defender que usar o setor privado só faz sentido em complementaridade com o público. Ainda, PSP garante que tempo de espera nos aeroportos melhorou.

observador.title: "É um erro culpar Bruxelas por falhas na política nacional"
observador.description: Lídia Pereira sublinha que os governos tendem a culpar a União Europeia pelas suas próprias falhas políticas. Também acrescenta que é essencial acompanhar o trabalho europeu de forma contínua.

observador.title: Casal britânico resgatado de ravina no incêndio de Almeria
observador.description: “Olha outra vez, tenta uma última vez”, foi o pressentimento de agentes da Guarda Civil que salvou dois turistas de uma ravina em Los Gallardos. Isso e o "esforço titânico" do casal para responder.

observador.title: O "bico de obra" da relação entre ministros e empreiteiros
observador.description: Luís Neves nega ilegalidades, mas falta-lhe bom senso nas obras. Já o Livre quer mandar no país à boleia do PS.

observador.title: Bernardo Silva: Mundial foi "frustrante" e "uma desilusão"
observador.description: Jogador português reagiu à participação portuguesa no Mundial, classificando-a como "frustrante". Infantino abre a porta a que próximo Mundial tenha mais nações.

observador.title: 9h. PCP quer chamar ministro da Educação ao Parlamento
observador.description: Partido pede um debate de urgência potestativo com a presença do ministro Fernando Alexandre. Ainda, a análise à troca de ataques entre EUA e Irão.

observador.title: Presidente de Moçambique quer CPLP mais solidária
observador.description: Daniel Chapo defende que deve haver uma "comunidade de solidariedade", promovendo o desenvolvimento e a coesão de cada pais da CPLP.

observador.title: Por que carga de água é que Luís Neves não mostra tudo?
observador.description: Os alunos (que agora desconfiam de tudo), o Livre (que acha que vai para o Governo) e o ministro da Administração Interna (que não explica tudo) são o Bom, o Mau e o Vilão.

observador.title: Eanes tornou-se Presidente há 50 anos. Nunca deixou de o ser
observador.description: Eanes foi o primeiro dos nossos Presidentes eleitos e, 50 anos depois, continua a ser o que tem melhor imagem. Como explicar a eleição do jovem general de 41 anos? E que papel teve ele na democracia?

observador.title: EDP alerta para fraudes com utilização de dados dos clientes
observador.description: Recentemente começaram a surgir mensagens no correio eletrónico com os dados corretos, como o nome e morada. A empresa alerta que esta nova forma de fraude é mais sofisticada.

observador.title: Jorge Jesus: De saltador de janelas a novo dono disto tudo
observador.description: Quem diria que o miúdo que descia por postes e partia fechaduras para jogar à bola ia chegar aqui? Entre "I love yous" de marmanjos e ameaças de pau aos jogadores, o mestre está de volta.

observador.title: Os quatro gigantes: quem vai agarrar a final do Mundial?
observador.description: Pela primeira vez, os quatro melhores do ranking dão a cara nas meias-finais. Vem aí o clássico Inglaterra-Argentina e muito título em jogo. França e Espanha também prometem aquecer a corrida à final.

spiegel.title: Ruth Moschner wendet sich an die AfD-Wähler unter ihren Fans
spiegel.description: Sie verstehe, dass einige ihrer Fans von den demokratischen Parteien enttäuscht seien, sie sei es auch, schreibt Ruth Moschner auf Instagram. Ihr Post endet mit einem eindringlichen Appell.

spiegel.title: Sacha Baron Cohen bringt Ali G zurück – und taucht in Wimbledon auf
spiegel.description: Prominente sind bei Wimbledon-Finals keine Seltenheit. In diesem Jahr mischte sich aber eine besondere Kunstfigur unter die Zuschauer – obwohl dieser Tennissport für Ali G. eigentlich nur »eine miese Version von Tischtennis« ist.

spiegel.title: Babys und Musik: Schon drei Monate alte Kinder reagieren auf Musik
spiegel.description: Eine Studie zeigt: Schon drei Monate alte Kinder reagieren auf Musik. Doch fürs rhythmische Mitwippen braucht das Gehirn mehr Zeit. Wie Eltern ihre Babys musikalisch fördern können.

spiegel.title: Hitze in Deutschland: Temperaturen können erneut auf 35 Grad steigen
spiegel.description: Das Wetter in Deutschland lässt wenig Luft zum Durchatmen: Es wird heiß, aber mancherorts auch gewittrig. Gegen Ende der Woche ist mit leichter Abkühlung zu rechnen.

spiegel.title: »Fulda Gap« im Kalten Krieg: Angst vor dem Atomschlag
spiegel.description: Im osthessischen »Fulda Gap« rüstete sich die Nato für den dritten Weltkrieg, auch mit Atomwaffen. Die Bewohner erfuhren, was Abschreckung wirklich heißt. Das prägt sie bis heute.

spiegel.title: Yellowstone-Nationalpark in den USA: Bison wirft Tourist meterhoch in die Luft
spiegel.description: Ein Bisonbulle hat in den USA einen Mann angegriffen und offenbar schwer verletzt. Es ist bereits der zweite Angriff dieser Art in kurzer Zeit. Experten sehen dafür einen konkreten Grund.

spiegel.title: Millie Bobby Brown Probleme bekam Probleme wegen einer Ofenkartoffel
spiegel.description: Englisches Essen muss man lieben. Die Erfahrung hat auch Millie Bobby Brown gemacht: Die britische Schauspielerin begriff in den USA schnell, dass ihre Essgewohnheiten andere Menschen eher an einen Unfall erinnern.

spiegel.title: Auswärtiges Amt bestellt russischen Botschafter ein
spiegel.description: Die Bundesregierung macht Russland für Cyberangriffe auf Deutschland, die EU-Partner und die Ukraine verantwortlich. Berlin und Paris bestellen nun die russischen Vertreter ein.

spiegel.title: Ebola-Ausbruch: Weiterer US-Patient jetzt in Deutschland
spiegel.description: Die Eindämmung des Ebolaausbruchs im Kongo wird laut Forschenden noch dauern, die eingeleiteten Maßnahmen zeigten aber Wirkung. Ein zweiter infizierter US-Bürger liegt in Frankfurt am Main auf der Intensivstation.

spiegel.title: Hitzewelle in Italien: Käsereien sorgen sich um die Qualität von Parmesan
spiegel.description: Die Hitze in Europa macht nicht nur Menschen zu schaffen, auch die Tierwelt leidet. Kühe in Italien geben zum Beispiel weniger und schlechtere Milch. Die Parmesanhersteller schlagen Alarm.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: Neue Gerüchte im Fall Folarin Balogun, DFB plant mit Millionenminus nach WM-Aus
spiegel.description: War die Begnadigung von US-Nationalspieler Folarin Balogun die Entscheidung eines einzigen Funktionärs? Das behauptet zumindest die britische »Times«. Und: DFB macht Millionenminus. Die WM-News.

spiegel.title: Cristo Fernandez: »Ted Lasso«-Schauspieler gibt sein Debüt bei US-Zweitligisten
spiegel.description: Fiktion und Wirklichkeit liegen in diesem Fall nahe zusammen: »Ted Lasso«-Schauspieler Cristo Fernández ist am Wochenende erstmals in der zweiten US-Liga aufgelaufen. Sein Start verlief jedoch nicht unbedingt glücklich.

spiegel.title: Neue Pläne der Regierung: 12 Euro für eine Packung Zigaretten – Tabaksteuer soll noch stärker erhöht werden
spiegel.description: Bisher plante die Bundesregierung eine Verteuerung des Zigarettenpreises auf 8,77 Euro pro Packung. Ein internes Dokument stellt nun eine noch stärkere Erhöhung in Aussicht.

spiegel.title: Volkswagen: VW-Chef Oliver Blume droht mit Abbau von 50.000 Stellen
spiegel.description: Lange ließ Volkswagen-Chef Oliver Blume die Beschäftigten über seinen Plan für den massiven Stellenabbau im Dunkeln. Nun erklärt er nach SPIEGEL-Informationen erstmals konkret, wie viele Jobs und Autofabriken bedroht sind.

spiegel.title: Fluggesellschaften: EU stärkt Entschädigungsansprüche und verbietet Zusatzkosten
spiegel.description: Wenn das Flugzeug viel zu spät ankommt oder gar nicht erst abhebt, sollen Verbraucher künftig leichter eine Entschädigung bekommen. Die EU verbietet außerdem manche Zusatzkosten, die zum Beispiel reisende Familien betreffen.

spiegel.title: Günther Jauch wird 70: »Wer wird Millionär?«-Quiz zum Geburtstag
spiegel.description: »Bildung lässt sich nicht downloaden«, sagte Günther Jauch einmal. Hier kommen 15 Fragen auf dem Weg zur fiktiven Million.

spiegel.title: Tour de France: Tadej Pogačar fordert wegen massiver Hitze Änderung des Rennkalenders
spiegel.description: Die Tour de France kämpft mit massiver Hitze. Eisbäder, Kühlwesten und Streckenverkürzungen reichen laut Tadej Pogačar, Träger des Gelben Trikots, nicht aus. Er würde gern einen »völlig« anderen Rennkalender aufstellen.

spiegel.title: Bangkok: Überlebende berichten von fehlenden Notausgängen nach Brand in Bar
spiegel.description: Die Flucht in den hinteren Bereich einer Bar in Thailands Hauptstadt wurde vielen offenbar zur Falle: Überlebende berichten, es habe dort keine Notausgänge gegeben.

elpais.title: El ministro de Exteriores francés sobre el artículo de Rajoy: “Es una estupidez, racismo o las dos cosas”
elpais.description: La ola indignación en Francia por los comentarios “racistas” del ex presidente sigue creciendo en vísperas del partido de semifinal que enfrentará a ambos países

elpais.title: Jean-Marie Le Pen debe de estar aplaudiendo a Rajoy desde su tumba
elpais.description: El expresidente español, al decir que en la selección de Francia no juegan franceses, conecta con una vieja tradición en el país vecino

elpais.title: “Las vigas se quemaban, cogí leche, agua, vinagre, cerveza, vino, lo que pillara”
elpais.description: Las dos horas de supervivencia de Juan Cremades en Bédar para combatir y vencer al fuego que acechó una de las casas diseminadas en el epicentro del incendio

elpais.title: Últimas noticias del incendio forestal de Los Gallardos (Almería), en directo | Sánchez promete recursos para la reconstrucción tras el incendio y reclama un pacto contra la emergencia climática
elpais.description: Moreno agradece al Gobierno el apoyo de la UME: “Siempre dispuestos, siempre capaces y siempre dando la cara” | El incendio de Los Gallardos se mantiene estable con un perímetro sin actividad

elpais.title: El PP de Madrid mantiene su respaldo al alcalde de Móstoles tras su imputación por presunto acoso sexual
elpais.description: El secretario general de los populares madrileños, Alfonso Serrano, ha repetido hasta cinco veces un rotundo “por supuesto” al ser preguntado si mantenía su apoyo a Bautista

elpais.title: El último recurso de Isak y Jonathan Andic ante el “sufrimiento” por su relación “pésima”
elpais.description: Antoni Bulbena, el psiquiatra que atendió a padre e hijo ante el bloqueo de la terapia, entrega mensajes de ambos a la jueza que investiga la muerte del fundador de Mango

elpais.title: Dentro de la Casa Blanca: así ejerce Trump un poder desenfrenado para dejar su huella en la historia
elpais.description: ‘Cambio de régimen’, un libro escrito por dos periodistas de ‘The New York Times’, desvela interioridades de la Administración estadounidense en el segundo mandato del magnate neoyorquino

elpais.title: Álex Baena: “Contra Francia intentaremos que sean ellos los que corran para atrás”
elpais.description: El futbolista del Atlético, introvertido pero cercano, habla de fútbol y de la armonía en el vestuario de la selección

elpais.title: Por qué De la Fuente confía en Marco Aurelio para pelear el Mundial
elpais.description: El seleccionador cita las ‘Meditaciones’ en sus comparecencias y se apoya en las ideas estoicas del libro del emperador romano en la gestión del equipo

elpais.title: La patria del balón
elpais.description: Francia seguirá siendo un rival descomunal aunque Rajoy se crea con la potestad de concederle o retirarle el pasaporte a media plantilla

elpais.title: ¿Cómo están los cruces del Mundial? Consulte los rivales probables de cada selección hasta la final
elpais.description: Un interactivo de EL PAÍS muestra el cuadro actualizado después de cada partido

elpais.title: Un incendio devora el bosque de Fontainebleau, a las puertas de París
elpais.description: Las llamas, que pueden haber sido provocadas intencionalmente, se originaron el domingo por la tarde y ya han consumido 800 hectáreas de vegetación del emblemático espacio verde

elpais.title: Estados Unidos afirma que sus fuerzas están “preparadas y posicionadas” para defender el estrecho de Ormuz
elpais.description: Trump asegura que el paso marítimo está abierto y Teherán insiste en que lo ha bloqueado, mientras ambas partes reanudan los intercambios de fuego por cuarto día en una semana

elpais.title: Europa vuelve a arrastrar los pies en las sanciones a Israel por la masacre en Gaza y Cisjordania
elpais.description: Los ministros de Exteriores analizan este lunes “opciones” para prohibir el comercio con los asentamientos ilegales de colonos, pero una decisión concreta se ve lejana

elpais.title: Ángel Víctor Torres: “En 2027 puede haber 500.000 nuevos nacionalizados con derecho a voto”
elpais.description: El ministro explica que no dará tiempo a resolver los 2,4 millones de solicitudes de la ‘ley de nietos’ antes de las próximas elecciones generales

elpais.title: Begoña Gómez, en manos de la Audiencia de Madrid
elpais.description: El tribunal provincial comienza a debatir varios recursos clave presentados contra la polémica instrucción del juez Peinado

elpais.title: El auge de Orriols que apunta el CEO devuelve al independentismo una incierta mayoría absoluta en el Parlament
elpais.description: El último barómetro acaba con un lustro en el que Junts, ERC y la CUP no conseguían asegurarse, como mínimo, 68 diputados

elpais.title: Detenido el periodista disidente marroquí Alí Lmrabet tras haber viajado desde España
elpais.description: El informador, inhabilitado por las autoridades de Rabat, reside desde hace años en Barcelona pero había visitado regularmente su país

republika.title: Legge elettorale, emendamento sul voto ai fuorisede troppo rigido. Il Pd: “Così è solo un bluff”
republika.description: La segretaria dei Giovani democratici Virginia Libero: “Non può diventare la foglia di fico di un'operazione di potere”

republika.title: Il dubbio di Sinner sulla strada verso gli Us Open
republika.description: Il n. 1 scioglierà le riserve nelle prossime ore. Sulla carta dovrebbe giocare prima a Montreal (2-11 agosto) e poi a Cincinnati (13-23 agosto) ma è molto probabile che decisa di dare forfait a uno dei due Masters 1000 per arrivare fresco a Flushing Meadows

republika.title: Il dopo Khamenei, cosa succede ora in Iran e che fine hanno fatto le opposizioni
republika.description: Dopo le rivolte di gennaio e le violente repressioni, la folla che ha accompagnato i funerali dell’ex Guida Suprema racconta un Paese dove il crollo del regime sembra sempre più lontano

republika.title: Sinner, blindato il numero 1 nel ranking Atp. Il vantaggio su Alcaraz (scavalcato da Zverev)
republika.description: La vittoria a Wimbledon ha garantito all'altoatesino la permanenza sul trono mondiale per almeno altri 2 mesi. Poi potrebbe rischiare ma dovrebbe fare malissimo nei prossimi 1000 e agli Us Open per essere scavalcato da Zverev obbligato, nel contempo, a vincere tutto

republika.title: La campagna politica per il 2027 è già iniziata. E ha una parola d’ordine
republika.description: La remigrazione, se da un lato rafforza Vannacci presso una parte dell'elettorato, dall'altro offre al centrosinistra l'opportunità di riattivare una mobilitazione progressista contro una misura che collide frontalmente con i principi costituzionali di uguaglianza e con il divieto di discriminazione

republika.title: Le Borse di oggi, 13 luglio. La guerra sostiene il petrolio e Milano azzera il calo con i titoli oil
republika.description: Sprofonda Seul, su cui pesa anche il crollo del settore tech e dei due produttori di chip, Samsung Electronics e SK hynix

republika.title: Sam Neill, addio al paleontologo di “Jurassic Park”. Era stata una delle star di “Peaky Blinders”
republika.description: L’attore aveva 78 anni. Tra i suoi film più celebri “Caccia a ottobre rosso” e “Lezioni di piano”

republika.title: Quando inquadrano Beckham
republika.description: Non salta una partita dell’Inghilterra, era a vedere gli Usa e pure l’Argentina: è dappertutto

republika.title: Bonifici tra parenti e amici: soglia, causali e donazioni. Tutto quello che c’è da sapere
republika.description: Cosa dice la legge nel nostro Paese sullo scambio di denaro e cosa interessa al Fisco: la coerenza con il profilo dei clienti, la giustificazione credibile e i pagamenti frazionati

republika.title: Milshtein: “La crisi è studiata dall’Iran per non trattare sul nucleare”
republika.description: L’analista israeliano: “Non è una crisi accidentale ma una strategia per arrivare a un’intesa sul traffico navale e non parlare più di atomica”

republika.title: Tensione Conte-Pd su Mosca. Provenzano: “Sta alzando il tiro”
republika.description: Il nodo della politica estera agita la coalizione. Per il membro della segreteria dem il Movimento “ha il problema Di Battista”

republika.title: Report, La Russa attacca Schlein: “Difese Ranucci, che imbarazzo”
republika.description: I dem replicano: non faccia il capo partito. FdI insiste sui legami tra le inchieste tv e il faccendiere. Il conduttore: “Nessun condizionamento”. E la redazione fa quadrato

republika.title: Il prezzo su Mps è giusto? Il “comandante” Lovaglio pronto all’ultima battaglia
republika.description: L’Ops di Intesa sembra mettere d’accordo tutti. Ma la questione ancora aperta è se gli azionisti di Siena saranno adeguatamente remunerati

republika.title: Il paradosso del clima. La “goccia” fredda che fa soffocare l’Europa
republika.description: Il contrasto termico provocato da un’area gelida nell’Atlantico crea una bassa pressione, che a sua volta risucchia aria calda dal Nord Africa

republika.title: Il Delta del Po in agonia per la siccità. Muoiono tonnellate di cozze e vongole
republika.description: Il fiume ha il 70% della portata in meno. Il cuneo salino in risalita rischia di danneggiare i raccolti. Il caldo blocca la maturazione dell’uva, vendemmie a rischio

republika.title: Il mondo si fa in quattro: Francia, Spagna, Argentina e Inghilterra, in campo vanno le migliori
republika.description: Le due partite mettono di fronte quattro diverse concezioni del mondo

republika.title: Preferenze, non c’è accordo. FdI presenta l’emendamento: Lupi lo firma, Lega e FI no
republika.description: Nervi tesi sulla legge elettorale: i voti segreti mettono alla prova la tenuta della maggioranza. I leader riuniscono i gruppi

npr.title: Sam Neill, known for 'Jurassic Park' and 'The Piano,' dies at 78, his family says
npr.description: In 2023, Neill disclosed he had been diagnosed with angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma, a rare type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Neill died on Monday in Sydney, according to a statement posted to the actor's social media page.

npr.title: What would it mean for Ukraine if it actually starts producing Patriot missiles?
npr.description: NPR's Don Gonyea speaks with Seth Jones from the Center for Strategic and International Studies about President Trump granting Ukraine permission to produce Patriot missiles.

npr.title: Fire breaks out at a pub in Bangkok, killing at least 27 people, officials say
npr.description: Footage shared online by first responders shows a huge blaze raging and plumes coming out of the front door of the pub in the northern part of the Thai capital.

npr.title: Toronto police looking for suspects after deadly shooting at festival
npr.description: At least two people are dead and at least four people are injured after a shooting on Saturday night at a festival celebrating Latin culture in Canada's biggest city.

npr.title: Alvarez's 112th-minute goal helps lift Argentina past Switzerland 3-1 and into World Cup semifinals
npr.description: Julian Alvarez sent defending champion Argentina into the World Cup semifinals with a long-range strike in the 112th minute against Switzerland.

npr.title: U.S. launches new strikes on Iran and Tehran attacks U.S. allies in the Gulf
npr.description: The U.S. and Iran exchanged fire for the third weekend in a row, with strikes stretching into Monday as Iran responded to U.S. attacks by targeting U.S. allies in the region.

npr.title: Palestinian aid worker who organized World Cup screenings killed in Israeli strike
npr.description: Palestinians are mourning Mohammed al-Wahidi, a beloved aid worker in Gaza. He was killed by as Israeli airstrike while en route to a World Cup screening which he organized.

npr.title: A veteran foreign correspondent looks back on a career covering conflicts
npr.description: For Reporter's Notebook we hear about what it takes to cover conflict over a decades-long career as a foreign correspondent.

npr.title: Most people who need glasses don't have them. Can the post office change that?
npr.description: In some towns in India, a visitor to the post office who's squinting at fine print might be asked: Do you want an eye test?

npr.title: Spain edges Belgium and will face France in World Cup semifinal
npr.description: Spain and France will meet Tuesday in Arlington, Texas, in a matchup anticipated for years. Neither team has lost at this year's World Cup.

nyt.title: Inside Israel’s Secret Operation to Cultivate Ahmadinejad
nyt.description: The yearslong effort to groom the former Iranian president as an intelligence asset culminated in a dramatic effort to take him to an Israeli safe house in the early days of the war. But the plan fell apart.

nyt.title: Oil Prices Surge After Iran and U.S. Trade Strikes
nyt.description: The renewed hostilities posed fresh risks to ships seeking to navigate the Strait of Hormuz.

nyt.title: Lindsey Graham’s Unexpected Death, and How Marco Rubio Is Running Venezuela
nyt.description: Plus, Sam Neill of “Jurassic Park” fame dies at 78.

nyt.title: Mercurial and Magnetic, Lindsey Graham Was a Force in the Senate
nyt.description: The sharp-witted South Carolinian repaired relations with President Trump to advance his foreign policy goals, was willing to cut deals with Democrats and tried to insert himself into every legislative fight.

nyt.title: Here's what we know about Lindsey Graham’s death
nyt.description: Senator Lindsey Graham died on Saturday night, a day after returning from Ukraine and four months before he was to face re-election.

nyt.title: Lindsey Graham Had a Complicated Relationship With Black Voters
nyt.description: Mr. Graham, a long-serving senator from South Carolina, was known for his ability to maintain relationships even with his political foes. But the support of Black voters remained elusive.

nyt.title: Japan Is Building a New Intelligence Agency With Help From the West
nyt.description: Facing threats from Russia and China, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is breaking with World War II-era limits on security.

nyt.title: How Putin Turned Japan Into a Den of Spies
nyt.description: Operating out of a Tokyo high-rise, a military intelligence unit finds the high-tech equipment that Russia needs to wage war.

nyt.title: Maine Democrats to Chuck Schumer: Stay Out of Our Senate Race
nyt.description: Local Democrats are warning the top Senate Democrat to keep away as they replace Graham Platner, and the candidates are giving his leadership in Washington low marks.

nyt.title: Civics Groups Are at Odds With Mamdani Over Push for Open Primaries
nyt.description: If a new effort to persuade voters to change New York City’s closed primary system gains steam, a potential showdown between its backers and the mayor awaits.

nyt.title: ‘We’re Fighting Satan’: The War to Save Bees From a Hornet Invasion
nyt.description: As yellow-legged hornets spread through South Carolina’s Lowcountry region, threatening the local honey crop, a state team of bee defenders is racing to the rescue.

nyt.title: Lebanese Hold Fast to Their Land Despite Threat of Long Israeli Occupation
nyt.description: Entire towns in southern Lebanon have been hollowed out by the war between Israel and Hezbollah. Some residents have stayed, fearing permanent displacement.

nyt.title: Sam Neill, New Zealand Actor Known for ‘Jurassic Park,’ Dies at 78
nyt.description: He appeared in more than 150 productions over a five-decade career but was perhaps best known for his star turn in the “Jurassic Park” series.

nyt.title: A Robot Army Remakes Ground Warfare in Ukraine
nyt.description: They began as supply mules. Now ground robots evacuate the wounded, hold trenches and even do the killing.

nyt.title: There’s an Injury Epidemic in Pro Sports. There’s Also a Recovery Revolution.
nyt.description: Athletes are pushing their bodies to astonishing feats, knowing that medical advances can heal them quickly.

nyt.title: With Threats Rising, Supreme Court Asks Congress to Increase Security Funds
nyt.description: Justices Amy Coney Barrett and Elena Kagan are scheduled to make a rare appearance at the Capitol to testify about the court’s more than $200 million request.

nyt.title: How Wealthy People Are Getting to World Cup Games
nyt.description: The skies above the Hamptons are packed with choppers headed to games, as “inequality is taking it right in the face.”

nyt.title: When Vital Weather Data Is Needed, Muppets Take Flight
nyt.description: “For the most part, the aircraft have their own souls,” said a pilot of the meteorological research planes, which are known as Kermit, Miss Piggy and Gonzo.

lanacion.title: Armando Olmedo, experto en green cards: “Va a haber más escrutinio”
lanacion.description: Conoce qué controles, demoras y posibles cambios salariales anticipa un experto para las empresas que tramitan una green card laboral.

phys-org.description: In a study recently published in the journal Environmental Research, scientists from the University of Sharjah have drawn renewed attention to contamination by polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs), a class of man-made chemicals formerly used as flame retardants in a wide range of products, including electronics, household appliances, vehicles, furniture and upholstery.

phys-org.description: New research by the University of Oxford and the Stockholm Resilience Centre at Stockholm University has revealed that most biodiversity commitments made by large, influential companies are not precise enough to enable society to evaluate whether they are making progress toward meeting their commitments. The results have been published in One Earth.

phys-org.title: RNA-only repair enzyme reveals how primordial life could have protected genomes
phys-org.description: In most modern cells, DNA stores the genetic blueprint, and proteins replicate, repair and build from those blueprints. At the same time, proteins require instructions from DNA to be made in the first place.

phys-org.title: World's first superconducting quantum heat engine offers path to larger quantum computers
phys-org.description: Recent improvements in our understanding of how the principles of thermodynamics apply in the quantum realm could give a boost to quantum technology, and a clearer picture of quantum thermodynamics could in turn enhance our understanding of classical thermodynamics. Now, Aalto University researchers have demonstrated the first cyclic quantum heat engine inside a superconducting circuit.

phys-org.title: More than 2,700 died as result of heat waves in England, researchers say
phys-org.description: At least 2,700 people died in England and Wales as a result of heat waves that struck in May and June, according to a study released Monday.

phys-org.title: China's 'Green Great Wall' tames desert growth, but scientists warn the fight is not over
phys-org.description: For half a century, millions of workers have repeated a task across the deserts in northern China: inserting forearm-length sticks into shifting sand, first in a row, then in an intersecting line, gradually forming a grid. Then saplings are planted at the center of each small square.

phys-org.title: Jellyfish videos reveal why science content sparks curiosity for some viewers
phys-org.description: It can be easy to get sucked into social media for hours on end. Funny, cartoony science videos may be especially interesting, but not to everyone, according to a recent study from the University of Georgia.

phys-org.title: Trees for hotter cities: New approach can bolster community input in meeting targets
phys-org.description: Efforts to plant more trees in cities could be boosted thanks to a new tool for planners and community groups, published by an international group of researchers. Residents, policymakers and tree officers in Cardiff, Milton Keynes, Edinburgh, York and Camden worked with academics to develop new advice to grow trees in a way that benefits both people and nature.

phys-org.title: Machine learning calibration of biosensors for microcystin toxin monitoring in freshwater
phys-org.description: Portable screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE) biosensors offer a rapid, low-cost way to detect microcystin-lysine-arginine (MC-LR), an extremely potent toxin produced by cyanobacteria during harmful algal blooms in freshwater. Even at low concentrations, MC-LR can damage the liver and has been linked to an increased risk of liver and colon cancer, and the World Health Organization has set a guideline value of 1 microgram per liter for MC-LR in drinking water.

phys-org.title: The public isn't bored with economists, management scholars and sociologists but engaging people has conditions
phys-org.description: For years, we've been told a familiar story: Social scientists such as economists, management scholars and sociologists talk, and the public shrugs. The claim goes that people don't find our work interesting, that our expertise is fuzzy compared with "hard" sciences, and that journalists and readers will always prefer the crisp authority of practitioners such as CEOs, consultants or politicians. Is that really true?

phys-org.title: How simple changes to PowerPoint presentations can make a big difference for learners
phys-org.description: Microsoft PowerPoint has become the default tool for presenting learning materials in classrooms, universities, corporate training programs, webinars and remote learning environments. But is it being used effectively? This question arises because learners face a major challenge. They try to listen to the speaker's explanations while simultaneously connecting them to the relevant visual elements on the slide, which can interfere with learning.

Improving their efficiency could reduce energy use and enhance performance across a wide range of technologies. phys-org.description: In drug discovery, building complex molecules quickly is the name of the game.

phys-org.title: Climate change leaves northern tree swallows more vulnerable than those in the southern US
phys-org.description: Tree swallows in the northern U.S. and Canada face the greatest risk from climate change despite responding to temperature the same way as tree swallows in the southern U.S., according to a new study led by Cornell researchers that analyzed nearly 95,000 nests across five decades. The findings, published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, reveal a critical timing squeeze for tree swallows in the northern half of the United States and Canada, putting them at risk.

phys-org.title: We assessed dozens of programs for men who use violence. Here's what we learned
phys-org.description: Domestic and family violence is an epidemic. In 2024, the prime minister declared it a national crisis. Official statistics show time and again that this violence is overwhelmingly perpetrated by men. This is unlikely to be news to most of us—we see it play out in our communities, online and on our screens.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: A Japanese Wake-Up Call for America
proj-syn.description: Japan’s deepening currency and bond-market woes should be a wake-up call for other countries that appear to be on unsustainable fiscal paths, not least the United States, as well as France, Italy, and the United Kingdom. After all, a crisis in one country often draws investors' attention to others facing similar problems.

proj-syn.title: The Israel-Lebanon Recipe for Never-Ending War
proj-syn.description: Lebanon’s political circumstances, together with Iran’s strengthened regional position, make Hezbollah’s complete disarmament highly unlikely. By conditioning Israel’s withdrawal from Lebanon on this outcome—but with no provisions about cutting Hezbollah’s Iranian lifeline—the new framework agreement is dead on arrival.

proj-syn.title: Why This Energy Shock Is Different
proj-syn.description: Unlike recent energy crises, today’s geopolitical shock is destroying supply rather than rerouting it, exposing the limits of the standard policy toolkit. Governments can mitigate its impact on those most exposed, but only if fiscal and monetary policy work in concert.

proj-syn.title: China’s Erasure of Tibet Is Accelerating
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the international community has stood idly by while China has systematically eradicated Tibetan culture and identity. With the authorities stepping up their assimilation efforts, Asia risks not only losing one of its oldest civilizations, but also facing a China that is bigger, bolder, and more powerful than ever.

proj-syn.title: Judging the Enhanced Games
proj-syn.description: If fairness in sports required a level playing field that all who wish to compete could afford, that would be a reason for banning expensive performance-enhancing drugs. But it would be a reason for banning expensive high-tech swimming suits and expensive high-tech running shoes, too.

proj-syn.title: What Is the Digital-Money Debate Really About?
proj-syn.description: Both the US and Europe are moving to create digital money, but neither has the right idea about how to do it. The key is to allow “narrow banks,” which issue money but not credit, to keep their reserves in central banks and provide capped interest payments to coin holders.

proj-syn.title: An Athenian View of American Democracy
proj-syn.description: At 250, America is now producing a mindless, raw power and exponentially growing instability. The possibility of catharsis that characterized the United States at its bicentennial is hard to envisage a half-century later—to the detriment of us all.

proj-syn.title: Low-Cost Solutions to Maternal Mortality Already Exist
proj-syn.description: As foreign aid declines, policymakers in lower-income countries must increasingly focus on making better use of scarce resources. When it comes to maternal mortality, that means investing in simple, proven, and affordable interventions for postpartum hemorrhage, pre-eclampsia, and obstructed labor.

proj-syn.title: Postmodern Economics
proj-syn.description: Eschewing the idea of a single truth, the recently deceased English artist David Hockney showed that the world unfolds before us in ways we cannot fully understand. After long clinging to the pretense of certainty, economists would do well to embrace the same insight.

proj-syn.title: Digital Public Infrastructure Is Now a Strategic Battleground
proj-syn.description: Digital identity platforms, payment systems, and data exchanges promise more efficient, inclusive, and responsive public services. But in an era of geopolitical rivalry and concentrated digital power, those same systems create strategic dependencies that governments can no longer afford to ignore.

proj-syn.title: Should the Bank of Japan Raise Interest Rates?
proj-syn.description: At the beginning of 2013, when "Abenomics" was rolled out in Japan, the yen was significantly overvalued, and looser monetary policy was badly needed. Today, the opposite is true, indicating that interest-rate hikes may well be the right prescription for Japan.

proj-syn.title: How Argentina Can Protect Its Resource Wealth
proj-syn.description: Alaska, Norway, and Chile recognized the economic and political risks that accompany commodity booms and established sovereign wealth funds to preserve their resource revenues. Argentina’s hydrocarbon- and lithium-rich provinces should learn from their experience.

proj-syn.title: Reinventing Development Finance
proj-syn.description: Faced with shrinking concessional finance and rising borrowing costs, Rwanda has worked with the World Bank Group to leverage limited public funds and risk-sharing instruments to unlock private capital at scale and on affordable terms. It's an arrangement holding important lessons for low-income countries that must do more with less.

proj-syn.title: Mamdani’s American Dream
proj-syn.description: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s Independence Day address was a perfect example of ideology in the positive sense of the term. It overturned both the right-wing populist narrative of the United States and the left-wing "woke" critique with a vision that has the potential to mobilize a majority.

proj-syn.title: How Vulnerable Are US Financial Markets?
proj-syn.description: Fueled by more than $1 trillion in borrowed money and rising leverage across the financial system, US stock markets may have entered bubble territory. Two developments could trigger a sharp correction: higher interest rates and a loss of confidence in the handful of tech giants driving the AI boom.

proj-syn.title: Concessional Finance Is Needed More Than Ever
proj-syn.description: As debt burdens rise and climate shocks intensify, sustainable financing mechanisms are becoming indispensable. The Islamic Development Bank’s new concessional fund offers a promising model for mobilizing the resources needed to protect development gains and invest in resilience.

proj-syn.title: Ruling Class Clowns
proj-syn.description: By the end of the 19th-century in the US, it was clear to all interested observers that market power did not automatically or even easily translate into political capital and cultural authority. That is why, unlike the oligarchs of our time, certain Gilded Age capitalists learned how to become a ruling class.

proj-syn.title: The Missing Ingredient for European Tech Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: Europe’s dependence on US technology companies is both an economic challenge and a strategic vulnerability. The European Union’s new Tech Sovereignty Package is a step in the right direction, but without equally ambitious efforts to curb market concentration, it is bound to fall short.
